fatal_errors: The proposed generic refractory HEA is not the target CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite, and it omits the controlled variation of Mo content.
The asserted 1000-1600 °C operating boundary conflicts with the target dry-sliding tests from room temperature to 800 °C and is not supported by tribological evidence.
The cited studies support high-temperature mechanical strength of refractory alloys but do not establish self-lubrication, coefficient of friction, wear resistance, or lubricant-film formation.

The proposed coherent-nanoprecipitate/dislocation-transmission mechanism misses the target mechanisms of Mo-induced lattice distortion, sigma-phase strengthening, MoS2/Ag lubrication, and high-temperature oxide/silver-molybdate glaze formation.
explanation: The response recognizes HEAs as possible high-temperature structural materials and proposes a basic comparative test, but it does not reconstruct the material system, processing, Mo-content intervention, test conditions, or temperature-dependent lubrication mechanisms. Its mechanical-property evidence is extrapolated to tribological performance without supporting wear or friction data. The claimed temperature and strength boundaries are largely imported from unrelated refractory-alloy studies, making the self-lubricating hypothesis insufficiently supported.
